How these numbers are calculated
  • Total Admissions counts admission records, not unique patients. Some patients have several records, so distinct patients are fewer.
  • Length of stay is the discharge date minus the admission date, in days (Tableau's DATEDIFF).
  • Percentage Abnormal is records with an Abnormal test result divided by all records.
  • Billing by Insurance Provider uses the patient-level LOD {FIXED [Name] : SUM([Billing Amount])}: each patient's billing is summed across all of their records, then averaged over the distinct patients each insurer covers, so repeat patients aren't double-counted. Names match exactly, case included. As with a FIXED expression in Tableau, a patient's total uses all of their records whatever the filters; filters decide which patients are averaged.
  • Average Over Time. The Tableau original plots the monthly sum of stay days under an "Average" label; this chart plots the true monthly average.
  • Filters. A click filters every other chart; the chart you clicked highlights your pick instead. The date range applies everywhere.
  • Data: Kaggle "Healthcare Dataset" (prasad22), synthetic patient records; this page loads the 8 of its 15 columns that the charts use.
